title: Canonical localization telescope is short exact
statement: For a small ringed site, an object U and a section f, let P be the countable coproduct of unit modules on the slice. Define d on basis summands by d(e_n)=e_n-f e_(n+1), and q by the n-th structure map into the sequential colimit defining the coefficient localization [def-weil-pbc-local-coefficient-localization]. Then the short complex with objects P, P, and the coefficient localization, and arrows d and q, is short exact. No condition on f or on products is imposed. Module sheaves are understood as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: The free-resolution theorem supplies a monomorphism d′ with the same basis formula. Coproduct extensionality and sectionwise linear-map extensionality identify d′ with the constructed d, proving monicity. The endpoint of that theorem is not used.

source.place: Tag 0997, proof of lemma-hom-from-Af, equivalence (1) and (3).

proof.text: The sequential-colimit transition identity gives d≫q=0. A map g from P with d≫g=0 satisfies g_n=f≫g_(n+1), exactly the cocone compatibility condition. The colimit universal property gives a unique factor through q. Hence q is a cokernel of d; it is epic and the short complex is exact. Together with monicity this proves short exactness.

mathlib_searches.query: In a category of sheaves of modules, the localization at a section is the cokernel of the telescope on a countable free module; derived internal Hom from that free module is the product of the target complexes.
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: SheafOfModules.free, iFree, hasLimit, free presentations and HasDerivedCategory.standard. These supply the elementary constructions, but none is the telescope exact sequence or the derived-Hom product comparison.

free, iFree and freeHomEquiv provide the coproduct and basis maps, but no telescope or derived-product comparison.
